patch.value: Current-main evidence: benchmark:scale:check ran the checked-in 10k fixture and preserved the fixed budget manifest. CLI create best/min was 363 ms against 310 ms; create peak RSS was 139,964,416 bytes against 115,184,640; claim peak RSS was 138,199,040 against 118,031,360. Read-path p95 remained below one second and all default outputs stayed below 5k estimated tokens. The implementation must diagnose allocation/startup causes and restore the existing budgets without raising thresholds, excluding paths, weakening iterations, or removing behavior. SDK parity and tiny-project responsiveness are guardrails.
10k scale gate regression: CLI create latency and create/claim peak RSS exceed fixed budgets

The deterministic 10k scale gate fails on current main under Node 26 because CLI create exceeds its latency ceiling and CLI create/claim exceed peak-memory ceilings; product p95 and token budgets still pass.

The unmodified 10k scale gate passes at least three consecutive runs on the supported Node baseline; cli.create best/min is at or below 310 ms; cli.create peak RSS is at or below 115184640 bytes and cli.claim peak RSS is at or below 118031360 bytes; no budget increase, exclusion, iteration reduction, or feature loss; SDK and CLI correctness/token checks remain green; before/after phase and allocation evidence identifies the cause.
pnpm benchmark:scale:check passes the committed latency, RSS, correctness, and token budgets without budget relaxation.
Current main fails cli.create latency plus cli.create and cli.claim peak RSS ceilings while all other reported product budgets pass.
